findings.summary: Resumed action-list execution is not exclusively admitted. After reconstruction sets state.resume, next_goal_call returns the persisted resume envelope without clearing or claiming that marker, before checking the in-flight fence. Two callers therefore receive the same interrupted call even though the new request lock serializes their admission checks. KernelCoordinator sends both envelopes to finish_goal_call, which has no execution-ownership guard. Both executions can observe an outstanding effect as absent and retry it concurrently, or both find no prior intent for an unstarted item and deliver it. Completion also attempts to release the same fence twice. This violates serial ownership and interruption-safe effect replay under behaviors 2, 4 and 7 and P6. Atomically claim resumed execution while retaining durable recovery state, and add an offline reconstruction plus concurrent-resume regression proving one executor, no duplicate effect, and no second fence release. The new concurrency tests cover fresh calls only.

Continuous independently records APPROVE for implementation subject 33e3a68fcfd5259484f4858c8366c20b331f01b4. Final independently records REJECT for resumed-execution ownership above. The inspected implementation addresses the previous Final finding concerning duplicate request acceptance, journal/queue ordering, and fresh-call admission through _request_lock; that improvement does not cover exclusive admission of resumed execution.

The supplied input_commit and subject_commit are identical full RC identities, and the Continuous artifact names the supplied distinct implementation subject. The committed implementation handoff names actor work_head_commit 7e089eb35a880fc613b7fd1e9ff4a59e87135d2a, rather than the supplied work_head_commit alias 33e3a68fcfd5259484f4858c8366c20b331f01b4. This difference is not itself a product finding: metadata-only materialization is permitted. Mechanical product-tree equivalence was not established using the available file-inspection tools; no Git or shell command was executed and no product-tree mismatch is asserted. Actual HEAD verification remains the deterministic seal's responsibility. Index, archive, and review-artifact inspection encountered truncated JSON lines, so complete feedback-history verification is not claimed.

The implementation handoff reports compileall exit 0 and 63 passing kernel tests; these are implementation-reported results, not commands executed by Final. Live Runtime binding and recovery, actual reply delivery, process stop/resume, full Session queries, merge reconciliation, multi-repo finalization, integration, deployment, and joint E2E remain unrun by this reviewer and deferred under the development-stage constraints. Their deferral is not grounds for rejection. This verdict does not establish production acceptance or whole-Goal ready_for_joint_validation.
